title.value: Revisiting Some Common Practices in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The title directly represents the central focus of the paper, which is to examine and potentially revise common practices in multi-agent reinforcement learning.
title.quote: Revisiting Some Common Practices in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

extractions.description: The paper examines cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) focusing on value decomposition and parameter sharing. It critiques these common practices under certain conditions and proposes the potential benefits of policy gradient methods. The theoretical insights are backed by empirical tests in various test domains, including matrix games and complex benchmarks like StarCraft and Google Research Football, aiming to improve MARL algorithm effectiveness.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is primarily focused on theoretical and methodological aspects of multi-agent reinforcement learning without explicitly addressing climate change or ecological issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We hope our theoretical and empirical findings can bring useful insights to the community towards developing more general and more powerful MARL algorithms in the future.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecologically-related sustainable development. Its focus is on improving theoretical approaches in reinforcement learning.
primary_category.quote: We emphasize that our work is NOT claiming for a new algorithm that is universally applicable. Instead, we attempt to provide concrete analysis to explain recent empirical evidence on PPO’s effectiveness and present practical alternatives of interest in certain scenarios.
